verdicts.statement: A presidential candidate must receive an absolute majority of electoral votes in the Electoral College to win the presidency.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that a candidate must receive an absolute majority of electoral votes to win the presidency.

verdicts.statement: The Electoral College has 538 electoral votes.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly refers to 538 electoral votes.

verdicts.statement: An absolute majority of 538 electoral votes requires at least 270 electoral votes.
verdicts.reason: The context identifies 270 of the 538 electoral votes as the majority required.

verdicts.statement: If no presidential candidate receives a majority of electoral votes, the Twelfth Amendment requires the House of Representatives to meet immediately to choose the president.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that the Twelfth Amendment requires the House to go into session immediately to vote for a president if no presidential candidate receives an electoral majority.

verdicts.statement: If no presidential candidate receives a majority of electoral votes, the House of Representatives must choose the president from the three presidential candidates receiving the most electoral votes.
verdicts.reason: The context states that in this situation the House chooses one of the top three presidential electoral vote winners as president.

verdicts.statement: If no vice-presidential candidate receives a majority of electoral votes, the Senate chooses the vice president.
verdicts.reason: The context states that when no vice-presidential candidate receives a majority, the contingency procedure assigns the choice of vice president to the Senate.

verdicts.statement: If no vice-presidential candidate receives a majority of electoral votes, the Senate must choose the vice president from the two vice-presidential candidates receiving the most electoral votes.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that the Senate chooses one of the top two vice-presidential electoral vote winners as vice president under the contingency procedure.
